confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for prices. The food and drink anchors rest on aggregator indexes and travel guides (mylifeelsewhere, Traveltables, and a few guides and listings), and these are crowd-sourced or partly dated. Reported figures were roughly $2.2 to $3.3 for beer, about $2.3 to $2.4 for cappuccino, about $2.7 to $3.1 for an inexpensive meal, and about $24 to $26 for a mid-range dinner for two. I set the anchors somewhat higher than the indexes because Koh Samui's tourist areas such as Chaweng and Bophut cost more than the island-wide averages. Cocktail is based on reported prices of roughly 100 to 200 THB, with higher figures at beach bars. Wine is the weakest anchor: no reliable restaurant price turned up, so it is estimated from the local beer and cocktail relationship and the high import duties on wine in Thailand. The three-course mid-range meal for two was not found as a precise figure and is a bounded estimate. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Koh Samui's tourist market. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect booking pages. They vary widely by beach area and season. The FX figure is the RBA observation reported in the search result for 18 November 2026, and the reciprocal conversion is left to the server.
comparable_city_reasoning: Thai island resort market, priced between Phuket and Krabi/Koh Phangan. Costs are above Bangkok and mainland Thai provincial cities for food, drinks and accommodation because of the tourist focus and island logistics, and below Phuket's premium areas.
